payload.title: [crypto-e2ee-7] senderId silently truncated to 32 bits (>>> 0) — two distinct logical senders can collide on a 3...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING crypto-e2ee-7 (low/crypto, confidence=medium, verify-votes +0/-1)

FILE: packages/core/src/e2ee.ts
LINES: 822, 923-932, 670-678

WHAT: The constructor stores `options.senderId >>> 0` (line 822) and deriveNonce uses `senderId >>> 0` (line 926); the v2 header field is uint32. Nonce uniqueness across senders sharing one epoch key depends entirely on senderId being globally unique per call. The seam itself never enforces that — it is a caller-supplied ordinal — and any value >= 2^32 (or two values congruent mod 2^32) collapses to the same 32-bit senderId. Two senders with the same effective senderId derive identical nonces for equal counters under the shared epoch key, which is catastrophic (key+nonce reuse) for AES-GCM.

IMPACT: If a future caller (FR-155 wiring) assigns senderId from anything not guaranteed unique in [0, 2^32), nonce reuse across senders breaks AES-GCM confidentiality and integrity for the whole epoch. The truncation hides the misassignment instead of surfacing it.

SUGGESTED FIX: Reject senderId outside [0, 2^32) at construction instead of truncating, and document/assert that the caller must assign a collision-free per-call ordinal (e.g. derived from the sorted member index). Consider binding the full memberKey into the nonce derivation/AAD rather than a caller ordinal.
